Training-history next-item targets already used for optimization measure fit and memorization; perturbing their prefixes does not make them held-out examples. Large shuffle/reversal losses therefore establish sensitivity, not useful temporal generalization. Proposed controls: recent-item-only prediction; item-transition scores aggregated over history; and order-insensitive history pooling or item similarity. Compare full shuffling with shuffling that preserves the last item, plus matched truncation/deletion, to distinguish order, recency and history-content effects. These are diagnostic recommendations, not proof that any architecture generalizes better.

Keep the benchmark unchanged: identical 200 validation users/category, positives, 99 unique negatives and seed across models, checkpoints and perturbations. Report category HR@10 and four-category macro-average. For paired 95% bootstrap intervals, resample users within each category, carrying every model/perturbation outcome together, then recompute macro-average differences. These intervals quantify user-sampling uncertainty conditional on fixed candidates and trained models; they exclude training-seed uncertainty and selection bias. Sampled HR can disagree with full-catalog rankings, so conclusions remain specific to this benchmark ([Krichene and Rendle](https://research.google/pubs/on-sampled-metrics-for-item-recommendation/)).

Predeclare checkpoint-level comparisons: diagnostic-versus-validation rank correlation, agreement on improvement direction, and consistency across categories. Correlated checkpoints are not independent replications; agreement on repeatedly consulted validation data is exploratory. Log all trials and checkpoint evaluations, and freeze diagnostic rules before further comparisons. Bootstrap intervals around the selected winner do not correct repeated-selection optimism ([Cawley and Talbot](https://www.jmlr.org/beta/papers/v11/cawley10a.html)). With splits fixed and hidden tests unavailable during search, independent confirmation must await the host’s final evaluation.
